where $\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{P})$ is the set of camera rays at target position $\mathbf{P}$, and $C(\mathbf{r}, \Delta t)$ is the ground truth pixel value [S2].

The claim states that $R(P)$ is the set of camera rays at target position P, and $C(r, Δt)$ is the ground truth pixel value. The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly defines $R(P)$ as 'a set of camera rays at target position P' in Equation 3. It also defines the loss function using $C(r)$ as the ground truth compared against predicted values. Furthermore, the notes and text clarify that the tone mapper predicts pixel values based on radiance and exposure time ($Δt$), and the loss minimizes the difference between predicted pixel values (which depend on $Δt$) and the ground truth pixel values (which are the result of the CRF mapping irradiance and $Δt$). Thus, $C(r, Δt)$ represents the ground truth pixel value for a ray $r$ with exposure $Δt$.
